did_you_know.text: Did you know? The vision of the temple was given to Ezekiel in the twenty-fifth year of the exile, fourteen years after Jerusalem had been struck down; the text notes that it was at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month.
Did you know? In the vision, Ezekiel was brought to the land of Israel and set on a very high mountain, where he saw something that looked like a city.
Did you know? The man who led Ezekiel looked like bronze, and he held a linen cord and a measuring rod; he was standing at the gateway.
Did you know? The man instructed Ezekiel to look with his eyes, listen with his ears, pay attention to everything that would be shown to him, and tell the people of Israel all that he saw.
Did you know? The wall around the temple was measured as one reed thick and one reed high. The measuring reed itself was six cubits and a handbreadth long.
Did you know? The outer court had a pavement with chambers all around it, and a total of thirty chambers faced the pavement.

Did you know? The north and south gateways of the outer court were built to the same measurements as the east gateway: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide, with chambers, porches, windows, and decorative palm trees.

Did you know? Beside the north gateway was a chamber where the burnt offerings were washed, and in the gateway’s porch were tables for slaughtering the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings.
Did you know? The inner court had chambers for the singers and the priests. One was for the priests who guarded the temple, and another was for the priests descended from Zadok who guarded the altar.
Did you know? The inner court was square, one hundred cubits by one hundred cubits, and the altar stood in front of the temple.
Did you know? The temple porch was reached by steps, and two pillars stood beside the entrance—one on each side.
